title: podman container prune: add --external support
body:
# Feature request: `podman container prune --external`

**Target repo:** podman-container-tools/podman (moved from containers/podman)
**Status:** Not filed yet

## Problem

Build containers created by `podman build` / buildah ("external" containers,
shown by `podman ps --external` with command `buildah` and status `Storage`)
can be left behind when a build fails or is interrupted. There is no built-in
age-based cleanup that can reliably distinguish abandoned external build
containers from active ones:

- `podman container prune` does not see external containers.
- `podman system prune --build` removes build containers without an age filter
  and is documented as unsafe while builds are in progress.
- `podman image prune --all --external --filter until=48h` (the command our
  prune timer ran) cannot be used either. `--all` includes tagged images,
  `until=48h` selects images by their creation date, not the container's,
  and `--external` allows pruning images that external containers still use.
  In our case it removed a pulled base image that was more than 48h old while
  a build was using it, and that build's container was deleted with it. The
  build failed with:

      error deleting build container "...": identifier is not a container

## Proposal

Add `--external` to `podman container prune`, honouring `--filter until=` on
the container's own creation time:

    podman container prune --external --force --filter until=24h

An age filter alone is only a heuristic: a build that runs longer than the
threshold could still be removed. The command should ideally skip external
containers used by active builds. It is unclear whether Podman can reliably
identify that state; if it cannot, the command would remain a policy-based
cleanup rather than a guarantee that active builds are safe.

## Workaround (tested in isolated storage, podman 5.8.4)

    podman ps --external --filter until=24h --filter command=buildah \
      --format '{{.ID}}' | xargs --no-run-if-empty podman rm --force

`podman ps --external` applies `until` to the container's own age (tested on
podman 5.8.4).

## Context

Came out of the builder prune timer fix in fedora-coreos-pipeline [PR 1410](https://github.com/coreos/fedora-coreos-pipeline/pull/1410),
where the review suggested filing this upstream. Once Podman supports it
natively, the workaround in `prune-container-resources.sh` could be replaced
with `podman container prune --external --force --filter until=24h`, subject to
the active-build safety limitation above.

Prior related report: [#14523](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/14523)
describes an interrupted build leaving a hard-to-remove build container
(Podman 4.1.0).

## Filing template

**URL:** https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/new?template=feature_request.yaml

**Title:**
```
podman container prune: support external (buildah) containers
```

The form has four fields. Paste each block into its field.

**Feature request description:**
```
Build containers created by `podman build` (external containers: command
`buildah`, status `Storage` in `podman ps --external`) are left behind when a
build fails or is interrupted. There is no built-in age-based cleanup that can
reliably distinguish abandoned external build containers from active ones:

- `podman container prune` does not see external containers.
- `podman system prune --build` removes build containers without an age filter
  and is documented as unsafe while builds are in progress.
- `podman image prune --all --external --filter until=48h` is not a fit
  either: `--all` includes tagged images, `until=48h` selects images by their
  creation date, and `--external` allows pruning images that external
  containers still use. In our case it removed a pulled base image older
  than 48h while a build was using it, and the running build's
  container was deleted with it. The build failed with:

      error deleting build container "...": identifier is not a container

We hit this on build hosts that run a periodic prune timer.
```

**Suggest potential solution:**
```
Support `--external` in `podman container prune`, applying
`--filter until=` to the container's own creation time:

    podman container prune --external --force --filter until=24h

An age threshold alone is only a heuristic: a build that runs longer than the
threshold could still be removed. Ideally the command would skip external
containers used by active builds. If Podman cannot reliably identify that
state, please clarify the limitation and intended safety model.
```

**Have you considered any alternatives?:**
```
Current workaround:

    podman ps --external --filter until=24h --filter command=buildah \
      --format '{{.ID}}' | xargs --no-run-if-empty podman rm --force

`podman ps --external` honours `until` on the container's age (tested on
Podman 5.8.4). `podman system prune --build` and
`image prune --all --external` are not suitable for this, for the reasons
above. The age cutoff is still a heuristic and does not guarantee that a
selected container is abandoned.
```

**Additional context:**
```
Podman 5.8.4. Downstream fix: https://github.com/coreos/fedora-coreos-pipeline/pull/1410
Prior related report: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/14523
Drafted with AI assistance.
```
